name: The Electron as a Rotating Bubble
description: A rotating charged oblate shell joining a flat interior to a Kerr-Newman exterior, a classical model of the spinning electron.
convention: We keep $c$ explicit and use $R_{\mu\nu}=R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$ with signature $(-,+,+,+)$. Tensor components apply in the smooth regions away from the shell.
history: Carlos A. López enclosed a flat spacetime within a rotating charged shell in 1984 [lopez1984electron]. The exterior is the Kerr-Newman gravitational and electromagnetic field. The boundary is an oblate ellipsoid with surface tension. López proposed this configuration as a classical model of the spinning electron. ¶ The shell's position follows from continuity of the geometry. With mass length $m=GM/c^2$ and squared charge length $q^2=GQ^2/(4\pi\epsilon_0c^4)$, its oblate radial coordinate is $r_0=q^2/(2m)$ [burinskii2002sources]. Its polar semiaxis is $r_0$, and its equatorial semiaxis is $\sqrt{r_0^2+a^2}$, where $a=J/(Mc)$ measures angular momentum per unit mass. The full polar diameter $2r_0$ equals the classical electron radius when $M$ and $Q$ take the electron's mass and charge [lopez1984electron, burinskii2002sources]. ¶ The shell rotates rigidly with angular velocity $\Omega=ca/(r_0^2+a^2)$ [burinskii2002sources]. An observer at rest in the flat interior measures an equatorial speed $v=ca/\sqrt{r_0^2+a^2}$. The speed approaches $c$ as the shell becomes more oblate. At the electron's angular momentum $J=\hbar/2$, with $\hbar$ the reduced Planck constant, the equatorial size is close to half its reduced Compton wavelength [burinskii2016bubble]. ¶ The gravitational matching assigns the shell zero comoving energy density and finite tension in both tangential directions [burinskii2002sources]. Its tension varies with latitude. The jump in the normal derivative of the metric fixes this surface stress, while the smooth exterior contains the electromagnetic stress. A vanishing interior electromagnetic field and the rotating Kerr-Newman exterior require boundary structure beyond an ordinary electric surface charge and current sheet [burinskii2016bubble]. A surface dipole layer is a formal option whose electromagnetic stress needs a specified regularization. In September 1985, Øyvind Geelmuyden Grøn reconstructed López's source through the geometry of surface layers [gron1985electron]. ¶ Static electromagnetic mass models use spherically symmetric charged matter. The density and pressure of a charged perfect fluid can have an electromagnetic origin, with a boundary matched to the Reissner-Nordström exterior [tiwari1984mass]. Ronald Gautreau constructed static spherical electron models in 1985 by setting the matter terms to zero in the charged fluid equations [gautreau1985electron]. Grøn connected repulsive gravitation in electromagnetic mass models to negative gravitational mass and also identified repulsion in López's spinning source [gron1985repulsion]. ¶ For $m>0$ and $q^2>m^2$, the rotating bubble has no horizon. The exterior occupies $r\ge r_0$, and a ball of flat spacetime fills the enclosed volume. The common time coordinate has a timelike gradient throughout both regions, so it orders causal paths across the shell [lopez1984electron, burinskii2002sources].

related.text: The gravitational and electromagnetic field outside the rotating shell is Kerr-Newman's [lopez1984electron, burinskii2002sources].
